name: Lucknow
about: Capital of the old Awadh court. The city's food and its architecture come from the same 18th-century kitchens and workshops, which is why a kebab shop and an imambara can sit on the same lane.

monuments.name: Bara Imambara
monuments.note: Central hall has no supporting beams; the Bhul Bhulaiya maze sits above it. Hire the official guide at the gate.

monuments.name: Rumi Darwaza
monuments.note: 60-ft Awadhi gateway, best photographed just after sunrise before traffic builds.

monuments.name: Chota Imambara
monuments.note: Belgian chandeliers and gilded domes. Lit up on Muharram evenings.

monuments.name: British Residency
monuments.note: Shell-scarred walls left as they were after the 1857 siege. Quiet gardens, good for a slow hour.

monuments.name: Chattar Manzil
monuments.note: Umbrella-domed riverside palace of the Nawabs.

monuments.name: Hussainabad Clock Tower
monuments.note: 67 m, tallest clock tower in India, next to Satkhanda.

food.note: Minced mutton kebab that melts without chewing. Eat with warqi paratha.
Sells out by early afternoon. Go before 1 pm.
Potato basket filled with tikki, dahi and papdi. Lucknow original.
Winter-only milk foam set in dew. Available roughly December to February.
Breakfast dish. Counter opens around 6 am.
Thick, saffron-heavy, served on a leaf plate.

name: Agra
about: Mughal capital under three emperors. Most visitors see the Taj and leave; the fort and the riverside tombs on the far bank reward a second day.

monuments.name: Taj Mahal
monuments.note: Closed Fridays. Sunrise entry has the thinnest crowds and the best light on the marble.

monuments.name: Agra Fort
monuments.note: Shah Jahan was imprisoned in Musamman Burj with a view of the Taj.

monuments.name: Itmad-ud-Daulah
monuments.note: The 'Baby Taj'. First Mughal structure in full marble inlay, and far quieter.

monuments.name: Mehtab Bagh
monuments.note: Across the Yamuna, directly behind the Taj. Best sunset viewpoint.

monuments.name: Fatehpur Sikri
monuments.note: 40 km out. Buland Darwaza, Panch Mahal and Salim Chishti's dargah. Half-day trip.

monuments.name: Akbar's Tomb, Sikandra
monuments.note: Resident blackbuck and langurs in the garden enclosure.

food.note: Ash-gourd candy. Try the angoori and kesar versions, not just the dry one.
The standard Agra breakfast. Spiced aloo sabzi with a fried bedai.
Book a table on weekends.
Salty lentil mix, the usual Agra gift to carry home.
Evening street lane, cash only.

name: Varanasi
tagline: Ghats at dawn, kachori by seven
about: Among the oldest continuously lived-in cities anywhere. Plan the day around the river: boat at sunrise, lanes at midday, aarti at dusk.

monuments.name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
monuments.note: Reachable through the new corridor from the ghats. Phones not allowed inside.

monuments.name: Dashashwamedh Ghat
monuments.note: Ganga aarti every evening around sunset. Watch from a boat to avoid the crush.

monuments.name: Assi Ghat
monuments.note: Subah-e-Banaras music and yoga at sunrise. Calmer end of the riverfront.

monuments.name: Sarnath
monuments.note: 10 km away. Dhamek Stupa, Chaukhandi Stupa and the museum holding the Lion Capital.

monuments.name: Ramnagar Fort
monuments.note: Across the river, with a strange, wonderful museum of old palanquins and clocks.

monuments.name: Manikarnika Ghat
monuments.note: Cremation ghat. Visit respectfully and do not photograph.

food.note: Breakfast staple with spiced aloo. Finish with a jalebi.
Soupy, sour, served in a clay bowl. Unique to Banaras.
Saffron milk froth, sold only in winter and only till about 10 am.
Thick clay-pot lassi with fruit. Expect a queue.
Roasted wheat balls with mashed brinjal and tomato.
Ask for meetha paan without tobacco.

name: Prayagraj
tagline: Where three rivers and three eras meet
about: Known as Allahabad for most of its modern history. Sangam, colonial civil lines and the houses of the freedom movement sit within a few kilometres of each other.

monuments.name: Triveni Sangam
monuments.note: Take a boat from Saraswati Ghat. Busiest during Magh Mela in January.

monuments.name: Allahabad Fort
monuments.note: Akbar's fort; the Ashokan Pillar and Akshayavat are inside the army-held section.

monuments.name: Anand Bhavan
monuments.note: Nehru family home turned museum. Closed Mondays.

monuments.name: Khusro Bagh
monuments.note: Three Mughal tombs in a walled orchard. Rarely crowded.

monuments.name: All Saints Cathedral
monuments.note: Gothic revival in white sandstone, locally called Patthar Girja.

food.note: Morning institution. Pair with their dahi jalebi.
A whole lane of chaat. Try the palak patta chaat and dahi bada.
Served thick enough to need a spoon.
Denser and less syrupy than the Bengali version.
Evening snack with strong kulhad chai.

name: Ayodhya
about: A pilgrimage town rebuilt around its temple complex, with a quieter riverfront on the Saryu that most day visitors miss.

monuments.name: Ram Mandir
monuments.note: Book darshan slots online in advance; phones and bags are not allowed in.

monuments.name: Hanuman Garhi
monuments.note: 76 steps up to a hilltop fort-temple. Visit before the main temple, as locals do.

monuments.name: Kanak Bhawan
monuments.note: Ornate gold-leaf interiors, quiet mid-morning.

monuments.name: Ram ki Paidi
monuments.note: Stepped Saryu ghats, lit up at night and during Deepotsav.

monuments.name: Nageshwarnath Temple
monuments.note: Old Shiva temple, the centre of Ayodhya's Shivratri celebrations.

food.note: Layered scraped milk sweet, sold by weight.
Hot jalebi poured over chilled rabri.
Cold almond and spice milk, best in summer.

food.where: Local bhojnalayas in the temple lanes
food.note: Simple satvik meals without onion and garlic.

name: Mathura & Vrindavan
bestTime: October to March, and Holi in March
about: Twin towns 12 km apart at the centre of the Braj region. Vrindavan holds the temples, Mathura the old bazaar and the ghats.

monuments.name: Krishna Janmabhoomi
monuments.note: Heavy security; leave phones and bags with your vehicle.

monuments.name: Banke Bihari Temple
monuments.note: The curtain opens and closes every few minutes. Extremely crowded on weekends.

monuments.name: Prem Mandir
monuments.note: Marble complex with an evening light show.

monuments.name: Dwarkadhish Temple
monuments.note: Mathura's main temple, centre of the Holi celebrations.

monuments.name: Govardhan Hill
monuments.note: 21 km parikrama. Start before dawn if you plan to walk it.

monuments.name: Vishram Ghat
monuments.note: Yamuna aarti at sunset.

food.note: Khoya peda with a slight roasted edge.
Standard Braj breakfast.
Served in kulhads with a layer of malai.
Thickened milk set in shallow trays.
Ask for the non-bhang version unless you know what you are doing.

name: Jhansi
about: A working railway town built around a hill fort, and the usual base for Orchha, 18 km away across the state line.

monuments.name: Jhansi Fort
monuments.note: Rani Lakshmibai's fort. Sound-and-light show most evenings.

monuments.name: Rani Mahal
monuments.note: Small museum of Bundelkhand sculpture inside a painted palace.

monuments.name: Government Museum
monuments.note: Chandela-era sculpture and coins.

monuments.name: Orchha
monuments.note: Just outside UP. Jahangir Mahal, Ram Raja temple and the Betwa cenotaphs.

food.note: Bafla-style baked wheat with dal and ghee.
Fried fresh through the evening.
Darker and chewier than jalebi.

name: Chitrakoot
about: Hill and forest country associated with the Ramayana exile years, spread across the UP and MP border.

monuments.name: Ramghat
monuments.note: Evening aarti on the Mandakini; boats available through the day.

monuments.name: Kamadgiri
monuments.note: 5 km forested parikrama around the hill. Watch for monkeys.

monuments.name: Gupt Godavari
monuments.note: Walk through ankle-deep water inside the cave. Carry a torch.

monuments.name: Hanuman Dhara
monuments.note: About 360 steps up, with a wide view over the valley.

food.note: Cheap, filling, sold through the morning.
Besan laddus sold in leaf boxes.
Simple satvik meal, served at fixed hours.
